answer: Like a glacier that only moves when its whole mass agrees, an agent economy can require every new identity to lock a stake that thaws over weeks, so fake accounts cost real capital with no instant return. A falcon-class auditor then randomly spot-checks clusters of agents funded by one wallet, flagging suspicious flocks before they vote. Finally, every agent must dock at a shared jetty — a public registry naming who minted and funds them. Operators who hid behind numbers suddenly stand in daylight, because accountability-free anonymity becomes expensive instead of cheap.
